prompt:
Original Japanese top-down pixel RPG asset visually inspired by Pokemon FireRed's overworld. Orthographic three-quarter TOP-DOWN RPG angle, front facing directly down to player, no isometric diamond or perspective convergence. Chunky deliberate pixels, crisp edges, restrained 24-color palette, dark colored outlines, sun from upper left, simple 3-shade clusters. Transparent background, no floor, no shadow beyond footprint, no text or logos. Readable when scaled down into a 16px-grid game. Match the attached reference sprites exactly in palette, outline and pixel density.
Match the palette, outline weight, pixel density and three-quarter top-down angle of the attached reference sprites exactly. Edit the attached outdoor tileset only; station and shop are style references. Keep all 32 cells and their exact positions, shapes and subjects. Fix the grass and ground tiles to use flat fills without light-to-dark gradients, dark border strokes, bevels or soft glow. Opposite edges of each square ground tile must wrap seamlessly. Both rails must reach exactly the edges of their square, with identical endpoint positions on opposite sides. Keep tree as one connected tree without a cross seam or gap through its center. Keep transparent gutters and transparent backgrounds around props. Increase pixel chunk size so each tile reads as exactly 16x16 logical pixels, tree 32x32. Keep the palette, object designs, camera angle and ordering unchanged. No text.
notes: Agent visual review at 1x and 4x. Fixed T indices 0..31; 32..47 transparent. Tree quadrants 17,18,19,20 reconstruct one 32x32 tree. Collision remains map-owned. Source v1 generated, v2 edited to remove tree seams and improve ground. Crop boxes remove generated gutters and ground borders. Palette sampled from generated source regions to retain green, red, blue, cream, brown and slate; visually matched against building references. Manifest and loader integration belongs to #1. Export source is the assembled 128x96 atlas (built from rawSource via export.cropBoxesByRuntimeIndex); tools/art/export.mjs re-quantizes it 1:1.
